tasks.title: Assemble a reply from chunks
tasks.description:
Implement `collectStream(chunks: AsyncIterable<Chunk>, onPartial?): Promise<StreamResult>`. Ignore `onPartial` for now.

- Read every chunk with `for await`.
- Add `choices[0].delta.content` to the text whenever it is a non-empty string.
- Remember `choices[0].finish_reason` when a chunk carries one.
- Skip chunks whose `choices` array is empty (the usage chunk at the end of some streams).
- Return `{ text, finishReason }`. If the chunks run out and no finish reason ever arrived, throw an `Error` whose message contains `ended early`.

The check feeds `collectStream` hand-made chunk lists: a normal stream with a role chunk, an empty delta and a usage chunk; a stream cut by the token limit; and a stream that stops without a finish reason.
nextSteps: Read the lesson section on what a chunk looks like.
Loop over the chunks and build the text in a variable.
Keep the finish reason when you see one.
After the loop, throw if you never saw a finish reason.
hints: A stream is not one response. It is many small objects, each with a tiny `delta` instead of a whole `message`.
The first chunk often has an empty content, and the last one may have no choices at all. Guard both before reading.
`const choice = chunk.choices[0]; if (!choice) continue` handles the empty case, and `choice.delta?.content` the rest.

tasks.title: Report partial text through a callback
tasks.description:
Extend `collectStream` so it calls `onPartial(textSoFar)` once after every chunk that adds text.

- `textSoFar` is all the text received up to and including that chunk, not just the new piece.
- Chunks that add no text (the role chunk, empty deltas, the finish chunk, the usage chunk) do not trigger a call.
- The return value stays the same.

The check records every call to `onPartial` for two hand-made streams and compares the list.
nextSteps: Find the line where you add a piece to the text.
Call onPartial right after it, with the text so far.
Run `node src/demo.ts` once task 3 is done and watch the answer appear.
hints: The chat window redraws the whole bubble each time, which is why it wants the full text rather than the latest piece.
The call belongs inside the same `if` that adds a non-empty piece.
One line is enough: `onPartial(text)` after `text += piece`.

tasks.title: Stream an answer from the model
tasks.description:
Implement `streamAnswer(question: string, onPartial, maxTokens = 200, client?: OpenAI): Promise<StreamResult>`.

- Call `client.chat.completions.create` with `model: MODEL`, `stream: true`, `max_tokens: maxTokens` and `messages: buildMessages(question)`.
- Pass the stream it returns to `collectStream` together with `onPartial`, and return the result.

The check streams an answer from the lab model and records every partial text, streams one with a small token limit that must end with `length`, and calls `streamAnswer` with a fake client to read the request you send.
nextSteps: Make the request with `stream: true` and the other options.
Hand the result straight to collectStream.
Run `node src/demo.ts` and watch both answers arrive word by word.
hints: With `stream: true`, the client does not give you a response with choices. It gives you something to iterate.
You already wrote the hard part. This function only builds the request.
Await the `create` call, then `return collectStream(stream, onPartial)`.
